# PUBLISHED ARAIM CERTIFICATION REFERENCE VECTORS — external oracle for
# kshana::araim_reference (tests/araim_reference_vectors.rs).
#
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
#   An independent transcription of the two published worked numerical examples of
#   the EU-U.S. Working Group C ARAIM Technical Subgroup reference airborne
#   algorithm. Every number below was read out of a PDF that was retrieved in full
#   and whose SHA-256 is recorded here; NONE of it is reconstructed, recalled or
#   computed by this project. tests/araim_reference_vectors.rs asserts that the
#   constants compiled into src/araim_reference.rs equal this transcription, so a
#   published figure cannot be quietly edited to make a check pass, and then runs
#   the engine against the published outputs at the tolerance the sources state.
#
# SOURCE 1 — the acceptance vector (self-consistent, current)
#   EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C, ARAIM Technical
#   Subgroup, "Reference Airborne Algorithm Description Document", Version 3.1,
#   20 June 2019. Appendix D, "Numerical example for LPV-200", eqs (79)-(84).
#   URL      https://web.stanford.edu/group/scpnt/gpslab/website_files/maast/ARAIM_TSG_Reference_ADD_v3.1.pdf
#   Retrieved 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200, 1165710 bytes, 35 pages)
#   SHA-256  7f42934488c5c2261363439fabd48385e39526df34d514f395e22b6990b6bdb7
#
# SOURCE 2 — the vector the research bibliographies cite (`wgc2016araim`)
#   EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C, ARAIM Technical
#   Subgroup, "Milestone 3 Report", Final Version, 25 February 2016. Annex A,
#   section A.IX "Numerical example", eqs (60)-(65), pp. 95-97.
#   URL      https://www.gps.gov/sites/default/files/2025-09/ARAIM-milestone-3-report.pdf
#   Retrieved 2026-09-20 (HTTP 200, 6124972 bytes, 121 pages)
#   SHA-256  156147e1e7aa9514cf7c9b7c7df9762daa7845981ec7037ad3e8aa5baeae13d8
#
# THE TOLERANCE IS THE SOURCE'S OWN
#   TOL_PL = 5e-2 m, "tolerance for the computation of the Protection Level", in
#   the list of constants derived from the navigation requirements (ADD v3.1
#   Table 4; Milestone 3 Annex A Table 24). Both documents require the output
#   protection level to be within TOL_PL of the solution of the protection-level
#   equation. It is NOT a tolerance chosen by this project.
#
# TWO DEFECTS IN SOURCE 2, RECORDED HERE AND DEMONSTRATED IN THE TEST
#   (a) Row 3's Up component is printed as +0.7477 in Milestone 3 and as -0.7477
#       in ADD v3.1. Milestone 3's own sigma_v,acc = 1.47 m is reproducible only
#       with -0.7477, so the 2016 print carries a sign typo. Both values are
#       recorded below (GROW as printed, ROW3_UP_SIGN_CORRECTED as used) and the
#       test runs BOTH rather than asserting which is right.
#   (b) Milestone 3 states N_fault,max = 1, which yields 12 monitored fault modes
#       (10 single-satellite + 2 constellation), but prints K_fa,3 evaluated at
#       2 x 57. Its EMT follows the 57-mode K_fa while its VPL and HPL do not, so
#       no single conforming implementation can reproduce all of its outputs. ADD
#       v3.1 prints the same example with 2 x 12 throughout and is consistent.
#       Source 2 therefore carries PL_REPRODUCIBLE no, and its protection levels
#       are reported as measured discrepancies rather than graded.
#
# FORMAT
#   Blank lines and lines beginning with '#' are ignored. Each record runs from
#   VECTOR to END. GROW rows are `east north up constellation_index` in the
#   published order; CINT/CACC are the published diagonals of C_int and C_acc in
#   m^2 (variances, not standard deviations). CONST_* carry the two
#   constellation-fault modes in constellation order.
